Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
177	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
178	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
179	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
180	
181	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
182	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
183	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
184	
185	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
186	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
187	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
188	  this draft). On a breach,
189	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
190	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
191	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
192	  (D2, ⚠️).
193	
194	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail, the exported GitHub audit log, change records and monthly reconciliation (S3, S8), JIT records, drift tickets and incident approval waits (S7); full register: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#register).
195	
196	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
197	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
198	incidents, plus detection.
199	
200	---
201	
202	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
203	
204	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
205	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
206	attacks.
207	
208	**On Papaya's stack**
209	
210	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
211	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
212	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
213	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
214	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
215	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
216	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
217	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
218	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
219	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
220	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed): [`03-rollout-plan.md`](03-rollout-plan.md), moved
221	  there with its items unchanged except syncs with the examples' findings (trail deny, allowlist,
222	  phase-2 version floor), and expanded with owners and checks [design]. Order (framing Q8): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow standing prod
223	  access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2). Phase 1 (0–30 days)
224	  makes the PR the default prod write path, with six hard prerequisites before standing prod write is
225	  removed; phase 2 (30–60) adds SCPs, the rest of the managed baseline and automated
226	  reconciliation; phase 3 (60–90) tests and reviews. The phase-1 load on 1–2 DevSecOps people is the
227	  main rollout risk [design; effort not estimated ⚠️].
228	
229	- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry.
230	- **Standards mapping:** ISO 27001:2022 Annex A (IDs recalled, ⚠️ R5.1), HIPAA Security Rule
231	  (📖 R5.2) and Vietnam law (📖 R5.4) are mapped per control area in the
232	  [compliance register](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference), with every caveat. "A named human approves"
233	  is Papaya's chosen way to meet these controls, not a literal requirement (⚠️ R5.7 #1).
234	- **Out of scope:** security of the production AI agents (A7a); noted as a follow-up.
235	
236	**Audit evidence.** Git history of policy files, monthly metrics, 90-day review minutes, the exception register and planted-injection reports; standards: [04-compliance-mapping.md](04-compliance-mapping.md#standards-cross-reference).
237	
238	**Cost / value.** Steady, small overhead for DevSecOps and the owners of deploy workflows. Compliance gets a managed system
239	with owners and review dates.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Gaps (not covered, or only as an open item, in `work/02-research.md`)
244	
245	| # | Gap | Layers |
246	|---|---|---|
247	| G1 | k0s: human authentication and RBAC (GĐ-4); placing the audit policy on controllers and shipping the audit log; the target OIDC trust on Papaya's k0s version (OD24 gives interim controls); break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 3, 6, 7 |
248	| G2 | Firebase Hosting deploy from CI without a stored token; break-glass when Actions is down | 1, 5, 7 |
249	| G3 | Human and agent access to GCP (roles, data access) | 1, 6 |
250	| G4 | Secret scanning, dependency check, SAST, non-prod data scanning on the Team plan | 5, 6 |
251	| G5 | Paging and alert routing; approving a PR from a phone | 7 |
252	| G6 | SSM Automation `aws:approve` (read in `work/03-options.md` §2, not in 02-research) | 7 |
253	| G7 | GitHub Actions log and artifact retention, and export | 3, 7 |
254	| G8 | Rulesets and environment settings through the API | 7, 8 |
255	| G9 | How Linear and Slack MCP servers authenticate | 4, 6 |
256	| G10 | OIDC subject customisation (`job_workflow_ref`) on GitHub Team | 1 |
257	| G11 | Closing provider/login bypasses on laptops without MDM | 2 |
258	| G12 | `pulumi up` flag reference for the prod allowlist | 3 |
259	| G13 | IAM actions for every data-plane read (S3, SQS, Step Functions, Secrets Manager, RDS, ECS Exec, Lambda invoke) | 1, 6 |
260	| G14 | Which state writes a Pulumi refresh preview needs on a DIY S3 backend | 3, 7 |
261	| G15 | Restricting a self-hosted runner to one workflow in a monorepo; just-in-time runners | 5 |
262	| G16 | Managing GitHub team membership as code; audit event for a membership change | 3, 7 |
263	| G17 | Who forms the L3 owner team and how many people (GĐ-1: never a single reviewer) | 3, 8 |
264	| G18 | Reading the live values of server-managed settings (API or local cache) to compare with git | 2, 8 |
265	| G19 | Required-check app and CI-agent app: review-event triggers, source pinning against same-name checks, hosting, private-key storage and whether those keys count against S2; the app's check that a risk-stop approval matches the stopped run's hash (OD18); reading Linear incidents and the schedule (OD27). The decision logic itself is examples E12 | 3, 5 |
266	| G20 | Emergency revocation at night: who can apply the revocation Deny SCP (management account) within minutes; `aws:TokenIssueTime` kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3) | 1, 7 |
267	
268	Open checks from `work/03-options.md` §8 remain open.
269	
270	## Owner decisions (2026-11-09)
271	
272	The owner answered the open questions of draft v3. English rendering; the original Vietnamese
273	answers are recorded in `work/session-log.md`.
274	
275	| # | Question | Decision |
276	|---|---|---|
277	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |
278	| OD2 | L3: must one approver be from the platform team? | Not necessarily; one approval procedure is agreed for all engineers, and the on-call engineer is enough. Clarified in follow-ups: every change involves two people, one who makes it and one who approves; the on-call backup only replaces an unavailable primary. Asked whether L3 should need more approvers than L2, the owner chose "L3 = 1 approver at all times"; in the agent's framing of that option, the approver must own the path. |
279	| OD3 | `CLAUDE.md` changes: L2 or L3? | L3, because the workflow must be consistent across the whole team. |
280	| OD4 | Move the rest of the managed baseline and the SSM check to phase 2? | Yes. |
281	| OD5 | "An agent does not approve PRs" only a process rule? | It is a rule: the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent. |
282	| OD6 | Scope of OD1: CI deploy credentials only, or also runtime scaling credentials? | CI deploy credentials (k0s kubeconfig/token, Firebase token in GitHub secrets) only, until it is checked whether k0s and Firebase can use OIDC. |
283	| OD7 | (a) If the on-call engineer writes an L3 fix, who approves? (b) Keep the read-only allowlist in phase 1? | (a) "While on call, never change the process"; clarified: on-call engineers only approve, and fixes are written by another engineer (the incident responder), so the approver is never the author. (b) Yes, as proposed. |
284	| OD8 | IAM/network/stateful changes inside a domain file: who approves the risk stop? | The stack's owners (may be the first approver); always two people. The L3 owner team keeps only the real L3 paths; Access Analyzer and policy packs compensate. |
285	| OD9 | How can one on-call primary approve any path at night? | The on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path; one primary + one backup. Normal-day domain review is a process rule with a monthly check. |
286	| OD10 | A PR touching files of several domain teams: split, or one approval? | One approval is enough (two-person rule kept); domain review on such PRs is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. |
287	| OD11 | Risk stop when the first approver is unavailable: may another owner of the stack approve? | Yes; it makes three people and is recorded as a deviation. |
288	| OD12 | `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed`: `true` or `false`? | Keep `true` (fewer prompts, relies on the sandbox, which arrives in phase 2). |
289	| OD13 | Confirm three agent readings: (1) OD8, who opens and approves the risk-stop approval PR; (2) OD9, scope of the on-call group; (3) L3-JIT, does the on-call approver count as service owner? | Confirmed: (1) the original author opens it and the first approver approves it; (2) the on-call group does not co-own process-defining paths or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves; (3) yes. |
290	| OD14 | Add the risk-stop classifier (`tools/risk-stop/`) to the canonical L3 path list? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes: it is a control, so only the L3 owner team may change it. |
291	| OD15 | Scope of the risk stop: risky diffs nobody looked at, or also malicious approved code? | Keep the current scope and state its limits; a separate prod preview role and a job split go to the phase-2 roadmap. |
292	| OD16 | Squash-only merges to `main` (needed so a PR cannot carry its own risk-stop approval)? | Yes; the cost is that PR-internal commit history is not kept on `main`. |
293	| OD17 | Deploy only the current tip of `main`, so re-running an old run cannot roll prod back? | Yes; added to the layer-3 "merge approval = deploy approval" conditions. |
294	| OD18 | An approval merged before a deploy stops, matched by a later change outside the stack's directory, is still accepted | Accepted as a stated limit; the approval-gate app (G19) is to close it by checking the stopped run's hash. |
295	| OD19 | Protect the names of SCP-exempt roles (`app-claims-*`, `cfn-deployment-*`, `github-prod-deploy-*`) so that only the IAM stack's deploy role can create or change them? (found while writing `examples/`) | Yes. Confirmed reading: "only the IAM stack" holds once OD20 gives the IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod Pulumi deploy". OD22 gives the IAM stack that role and subject in phase 1. |
296	| OD20 | Code in the deploy job (install scripts, Pulumi program, Serverless plugins) can request the job's OIDC token for either prod deploy role: fix now or roadmap? | Roadmap phase 2, together with OD15: a build job without `id-token`, and per-role environments (different OIDC subjects) or `job_workflow_ref`. Until then it is a stated limit. **Superseded in timing by OD22:** per-environment roles move to phase 1. |
297	| OD21 | Phase 1 lets built-in read-only commands (`cat`, `head` …) read `~/.aws` without a prompt, and allow rules skip the auto-mode classifier: add keys to the phase-1 subset? | Yes: add a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` (examples finding 19). |
298	
299	**Fixes after the independent review** (`work/07-review.md`; proposals and the owner's choices in
300	`work/08-fix-proposals.md`, documentation checks in `work/09-fix-research.md`). The owner accepted
301	every proposal on 2026-11-09:
302	
303	| # | Review finding | Decision |
304	|---|---|---|
305	| OD22 | Approved code runs with a prod deploy role, which can change SCP-exempt roles (review A-1) | Moves OD20 into phase 1: the IAM stack gets its own environment `production-iam` and role; domain deploy roles change only `svc-*` roles under a fixed permissions boundary; no install scripts in deploy and preview jobs except a reviewed allowlist (L3 path); agent review on every PR touching infrastructure code. The separate preview role (OD15) stays in phase 2. |
306	| OD23 | Identity Center administrators and `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` can grant prod write outside the design (review C-4) | Identity Center permission sets and assignments as code (L3 owner team only) with alerts on other changes; an SCP denies `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` in the prod OU; member-account root credentials removed; a named management-account group. |
307	| OD24 | The long-lived k0s deploy credential is undetectable if leaked, on the cluster that runs AI agents reading partner documents (review A-4) | Phase 1: a namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token without Secret, exec, log, token, RBAC or delete rights; `production-k0s` environment required; Kubernetes API audit log. Target: k0s trusts GitHub OIDC directly. |
308	| OD25 | An approval proves a GitHub account, not a named person; an agent can approve through its engineer's login (review C-1) | Required 2FA, a login register fed by HR with quarterly review, restricted personal access tokens; from phase 1, managed deny rules for `gh pr review`, `gh api …reviews…` and the `gh` token file (hygiene); Enterprise Cloud (SAML, environment reviewers, audit-log streaming) is listed with its price as a decision for Papaya. |
309	| OD26 | A component that runs on every laptop (plugin, hook, local MCP server) can give an attacker many logins at once, so author ≠ approver is no longer two independent people (review A-2, A-3) | Threat T23; marketplace pinned to a protected release tag, every plugin (internal too) pinned by `sha`, auto-update off; local MCP servers only as immutable artifacts (image digest or pinned plugin); approval-gate app flags suspicious approvals; **process paths need two L3 owner team members** (partly reverses OD2, ADR-0012). |
310	| OD27 | The `incident` label opens cross-domain approval, and anyone with Triage can apply it (review E-2) | The approval-gate app counts an on-call approval for another team's file only with an open incident and the approver on shift; the label alone grants nothing; every `incident` PR is in the monthly report. Consequence: on normal days a cross-team PR needs an owner of each team (changes the effect of OD10; ADR-0012). The app becomes a hard phase-1 prerequisite. |

1	# Engineer guide: working with Claude Code at Papaya
     2	
     3	> Status: a summary of the approved framework; it adds no rule · Updated: 2026-11-09 · Builds on
     4	> [`01-framework.md`](01-framework.md)
     5	
     6	This page answers one question: **what changes in my working day?** Each section says what you do,
     7	who approves, and how long it takes. The rules and their sources are in the framework layer linked
     8	from each section; if this page and the framework differ, the framework wins. Times are targets from
     9	the success criteria (S-n) or estimates marked ⚠️.
    10	
    11	## The short version
    12	
    13	- **Non-prod is yours.** Build, deploy and debug in non-prod with the agent, with no new approval (S4),
    14	  once a store has been scanned for real data (until then it follows the real-data rule, section 5).
    15	- **Prod reads are metrics and metadata.** No standing prod write for anyone, you included.
    16	- **Every prod change is a pull request.** One code owner who is not you approves; CI applies it.
    17	- **In an incident the path is the same, with faster people:** an on-call approver, 24/7.
    18	- **Real customer data, new tools and break-glass need a request.** Each has a named approver and a time limit.
    19	
    20	## 1. Daily development (non-prod)
    21	
    22	- **What you do:** use Claude Code as you do today, with non-prod roles. Manual permission mode is the
    23	  default; you may switch to auto mode (D1). Commands that run inside the sandbox run without a prompt
    24	  (phase 2, OD12).
    25	- **Approval:** none (risk level L1).
    26	- **What is different:** the organisation's managed settings apply to everyone; bypass mode is
    27	  removed; plugins and MCP servers come from the catalogue only (section 6). From phase 2 the sandbox
    28	  hides credentials and blocks Unix sockets, so `git push`, `gh`, Docker and private-registry `npm ci` fail inside it: run
    29	  them yourself at the `!` prompt. Using `--restricted` is recommended (D3).
    30	- **From phase 2 you will also notice** (layer 2, examples E8): each `aws`, `pulumi` or `serverless`
    31	  call asks you first, in auto mode too; each WebFetch asks; your own and the project's permission
    32	  rules are ignored, so prompts may rise; sign-in is locked to Papaya's organisation (API-key sessions
    33	  are refused) and the minimum Claude Code version rises; on macOS, servers on localhost fail inside
    34	  the sandbox; native Windows is not supported (use WSL2).
    35	- **Layer:** [2](01-framework.md#layer-2--agent-runtime-controls).
    36	
    37	## 2. Reading prod
    38	
    39	- **What you do:** with `ProdReadMetadata` (1-hour session) you and your agent read metrics, metadata
    40	  and logs that are redacted at source. Lambda configuration is readable per service once its secrets
    41	  are resolved at runtime; until then, read timeout and memory from the IaC code.
    42	- **Approval:** none (L0).
    43	- **Cost to know:** in the first months, raw logs of services not yet redacted are not readable
    44	  without a data-read request (section 5). This is the largest cost of the transition.
    45	- **Remember:** the agent uses **your** AWS SSO session, so it can do whatever you can (layer 1). Keep
    46	  the portal session short.
    47	- **Layer:** [1](01-framework.md#layer-1--identity-and-access).
    48	
    49	## 3. Shipping a prod change
    50	
    51	1. Write the change as code (Pulumi, `serverless.yml`, Kubernetes manifests) and preview it on non-prod.
    52	2. Push the branch and open a pull request. The PR runs secret scanning, dependency checks and SAST
    53	   (S10), and previews non-prod only.
    54	3. One code owner of the changed files approves. You cannot approve your own PR, and the approver may
    55	   not be the last person who pushed. An agent never approves a PR (OD5); managed settings also
    56	   block `gh pr review` for agents (OD25).
    57	   - Domain code and stacks: your domain team. Members of the on-call group are co-owners, but
    58	     their approval counts for another team's files only on an incident PR while they are on shift;
    59	     the approval-gate check enforces it (OD27). A PR that touches several teams' files needs an
    60	     owner of each.
    61	   - Process files (`.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, the catalogue, the SCP stack,
    62	     `tools/risk-stop/`, `tools/ci/`, `oncall/`): **two** members of the L3 owner team (OD26).
    63	4. Merge (squash only). The deploy job previews prod and applies the change.
    64	5. **If the deploy stops at the risk stop** (stateful replace or delete, IAM, network, a policy
    65	   finding): open a second PR that adds only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<stopped commit>.yaml` with the
    66	   hash from the job summary. By default the first approver approves it; if they are unavailable,
    67	   another owner of the stack does, which is recorded as a deviation (OD13, OD11). Merging it deploys
    68	   if the new prod preview has the same hash. While the stack is stopped, later merges to it stop too.
    69	
    70	- **Time:** same working day from PR to prod; approval wait ≤ 1 hour in working hours (S4 targets).
    71	- **What CI does differently (OD22):** npm install scripts do not run in preview and deploy jobs;
    72	  if a package needs its script, ask the L3 owner team to add it to `tools/ci/allowed-install-scripts.txt`.
    73	  A stack may create IAM roles for its own services only as `svc-*` roles with the standard
    74	  permissions boundary; roles that read claim data (`app-claims-*`) are created in the IAM stack
    75	  and referenced by ARN. PRs that touch infrastructure code also get an automated agent review,
    76	  which is advice, not an approval.
    77	- **Layer:** [3](01-framework.md#layer-3--change-workflow-by-risk-level); diagram
    78	  [`01-change-workflow`](../diagrams/01-change-workflow.svg).
    79	
    80	## 4. An incident at 2 a.m.
    81	
    82	You are the **incident responder**. The **on-call approver** only approves; they never write the fix (OD7).
    83	
    84	1. Start an incident-analysis session with read-only roles, in an empty scratch directory outside
    85	   the repository: `--restricted --tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"` (no WebFetch; Bash can still reach
    86	   the network). Read metrics and redacted logs.
    87	2. Open (or find) the incident issue in Linear. Make the fix in a normal session, preview on
    88	   non-prod, and open a PR labelled `incident` that links the issue: the on-call approval counts
    89	   only while the issue is open and the approver is on shift (OD27).
    90	3. Call the on-call approver (phone in phase 1; routed alerts from phase 2). They review and approve.
    91	   If they find a problem, you push the fix and they approve again.
    92	4. Merge; the deploy job applies the change.
    93	
    94	- **Time:** target ≤ 15 min waiting for approval (S7); 11–46 min from decision to apply is an
    95	  estimate (⚠️), measured first during rollout against a 30-minute target.
    96	- **Blockers to know:** a risky change already waiting on `main` blocks your fix for that stack until
    97	  it is approved or reverted; at night, process files (workflows, `CLAUDE.md`, catalogue) wait for the
    98	  L3 owner team, or the JIT fallback applies.
    99	- **Only if the PR path cannot be used** (GitHub Actions down, broken pipeline, an operation not in
   100	  IaC): end your AWS portal session and sign in fresh, then request a JIT grant in the incident
   101	  channel outside GitHub, with the exact commands. The on-call approver approves before the grant.
   102	  You get `InfraOperator-<service>` (1-hour role session; the real window can approach 2 h) and type
   103	  the commands yourself, in a terminal **without an agent**. Afterwards your commands are compared
   104	  with CloudTrail (by hand in phase 1, by a job from phase 2), and you open a PR that codifies the change.
   105	- **Layers:** [3](01-framework.md#layer-3--change-workflow-by-risk-level),
   106	  [7](01-framework.md#layer-7--observability-audit-incident-response-and-break-glass); diagram
   107	  [`03-incident-lane`](../diagrams/03-incident-lane.svg).
   108	
   109	## 5. Reading real customer data
   110	
   111	- **What you do:** end your AWS portal session and sign in fresh, then request it with one tenant,
   112	  purpose, store, time window and the agreement that covers it. You get a data-read role for 1 hour.
   113	  After reading one tenant's data, do not post to shared places without review.
   114	- **Approval:** an approver who is not you, plus the data owner. At night the on-call approver
   115	  approves alone, and the data owner reviews it the next working day.
   116	- **PHI (medical records):** you read it yourself, in a terminal **without an agent**; give the agent
   117	  only a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
   118	  it. Partner-uploaded claim documents never go into an agent session raw: reproduce with synthetic
   119	  documents, or de-identify them first.
   120	- **Non-prod** should hold no real data; a store not yet scanned follows this section's rule.
   121	- **Layer:** [6](01-framework.md#layer-6--data-protection-and-prompt-injection-defence).
   122	
   123	## 6. Adding a plugin or MCP server
   124	
   125	- **What you do:** open a request with what the tool reads, where it sends data and which write
   126	  tools it needs. A local MCP server is admitted only as a container image pinned by digest or as
   127	  code inside a pinned plugin, not as `npx -y <package>` (OD26). Keep your GitHub CLI token in the
   128	  system credential store (`gh auth status` shows where it is). A catalogue entry is added by a PR with a review record (examples
   129	  [`reviews/`](../examples/claude/marketplace/reviews/)).
   130	- **Approval:** two members of the L3 owner team (the catalogue is a process path, OD26).
   131	- **Time:** decided within 5 working days (S6).
   132	- **Not allowed:** installing a plugin or MCP server outside the catalogue, or sideloading one with
   133	  command-line flags.
   134	- **Layer:** [4](01-framework.md#layer-4--supply-chain-for-mcp-servers-and-plugins).
   135	
   136	## 7. When you are the on-call approver
   137	
   138	- You are on a named 24/7 schedule: a primary and a backup. The primary approves; the backup steps in
   139	  only if the primary is unavailable (OD2).
   140	- While on call you **only approve**: you do not write fixes or request JIT grants (OD7). A night
   141	  incident therefore needs two people awake: the responder and you.
   142	- Target: approve within 15 minutes (S7). Approve JIT only when the PR path cannot be used, and record
   143	  why you refuse it otherwise.

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-11-09

a named human who reviewed and approved it. "Most engineers' profiles can reach production" (brief), and deploys from laptops are assumed

review is highest.

| D. Hosted agent with its own identity | Clean separation | New platform; does not remove the need for approval |

decision to apply.

52	# ADR-0002: Nobody holds standing prod write; in prod, the engineer's (and so the agent's) only standing role reads metadata
53	
54	- **Status:** Accepted
55	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
56	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (Options §9; D2)
57	- **Scope:** AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets and SCPs on the prod OU; k0s, GCP and Firebase by the same principle
58	
59	## 1. Context
60	
61	On a laptop the agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and one portal session reaches every role
62	assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate "agent"
63	permission set therefore does not separate the agent from the engineer (⚠️ R2.9 #1). Whatever the
64	engineer holds, the agent holds.
65	
66	## 2. Options considered
67	
68	| Option | Pros | Cons |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| A. Separate agent permission set, engineer keeps write | Looks like least privilege | Same SSO cache: the agent can still assume the write role |
71	| B. No standing prod write for anyone; `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role | Agent cannot write prod with the engineer's identity | Engineers also lose direct writes and raw-log reads |
72	| C. Separate OS user or container for agent sessions | Real separation of credentials | More setup; planned for phase 3 only |
73	
74	## 3. Decision
75	
76	Option B. Prod is written only by the CI pipeline role, or by an approved, time-boxed JIT grant
77	(ADR-0005). The standing prod role is `ProdReadMetadata` [design name]: metrics, redacted log groups,
78	configuration of services whose secrets are resolved at runtime; no data-plane reads of claim stores;
79	1-hour role session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). From phase 2, SCPs on the prod OU deny data-plane reads and
80	direct Lambda updates except for named roles (pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4, R4.6 #3). Option C follows in phase 3.
81	
82	## 4. Consequences
83	
84	- **Positive:** once standing write and broad read roles are removed (end of phase 1), an agent,
85	  even a manipulated one, cannot write prod AWS or read AWS claim stores with the engineer's standing
86	  identity (data-plane action list ⚠️ G13); k0s and GCP follow the same principle, mechanisms open
87	  (G1, G3). In non-prod the agent keeps broad rights (`NonProdDeveloper`, ADR-0010 L1). Compliance gets least privilege enforced by IAM (S1).
88	- **Negative / trade-offs:** during the transition, engineers lose raw logs and configuration of
89	  services not yet redacted. Configuration values then come from the IaC code; raw logs need a
90	  data-read grant in an incident. Process rules remain where
91	  IAM cannot separate engineer and agent: no agent in the JIT terminal (D2).
92	- **Risks & how we watch them:** SSO-token theft during a session could open later grants (⚠️);
93	  mitigations [design] are a short portal session and a fresh sign-in before a grant. The data-plane action
94	  list is incomplete (⚠️ G13). Identity Center assignment export is reviewed quarterly.
95	- **Next steps:** phase 1 removes broad read roles only after the minimal real-data read flow works,
96	  then removes standing prod write once its prerequisites are in place.
97	
98	## 5. References
99	
100	- Framework layer 1, layer 2 ("Trade-off on AWS credentials"), layer 8 rollout.
101	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0005, ADR-0009.

103	# ADR-0003: The merge to `main` is the approval gate: two people, code owners, on-call co-ownership
104	
105	- **Status:** Accepted
106	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
107	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-5, GĐ-8, GĐ-11; OD2, OD5, OD7, OD9, OD10, OD13)
108	- **Scope:** GitHub monorepo rulesets, CODEOWNERS, `production` environment, on-call schedule
109	
110	## 1. Context
111	
112	Papaya is assumed to be on GitHub Team (GĐ-5), where environment required reviewers do not exist for
113	private repositories (📖 R3.1.2), so the approval must happen before the deploy job. Incidents need an
114	approver within 15 minutes, 24/7 (S7), and code-owner review requires an approval from an owner of the files (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7;
115	per-file behaviour ⚠️).
116	
117	## 2. Options considered
118	
119	| Option | Pros | Cons |
120	|---|---|---|
121	| A. Upgrade to Enterprise for environment reviewers | Approval sits next to the deploy | Cost; not assumed (GĐ-5) |
122	| B. Merge to `main` as the gate; `production` limited to `main` | Works on Team; the approver sees the code that will be applied | Nobody sees the prod diff before apply (partly handled by ADR-0004) |
123	| C. More approvers for high-risk changes | More eyes | Slower; the owner wants two people per change |
124	
125	## 3. Decision
126	
127	Option B. Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
128	approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
129	push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5); branch up to date, since there is no merge queue
130	(⚠️ R4.6 #1). `production` accepts only `main` (📖 R3.1.3).
131	
132	- **Merge = deploy approval** only if the reusable deploy workflow alone references `production`,
133	  with no ref/SHA inputs, no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers, one
134	  concurrency group per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4; ⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c).
135	- **Two people per change:** one makes it, one approves it; the approver is always an engineer,
136	  never an agent (OD2, OD5). L3 changes need one approver too, who must own the path.
137	- **Incidents:** on-call engineers only approve; an incident responder writes the fix (OD7).
138	- **Night coverage:** an on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path in CODEOWNERS; one
139	  primary, one backup (OD9). It does not co-own process-defining paths (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS,
140	  agent config, catalogue) or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves (OD13); IAM-only
141	  stacks are deployable, so it co-owns them with the L3 owner team.
142	- **Agent review:** an independent agent may post an automated review; it never counts as an
143	  approval (GĐ-11).
144	- **Cross-team PRs:** one approval is enough (OD10).
145	
146	## 4. Consequences
147	
148	- **Positive:** four-eyes enforced by GitHub, not by the agent; one rule for normal days and incidents.
149	- **Negative / trade-offs:** GitHub accepts an approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so the
150	  on-call group can approve another domain's PR; domain review on normal days is a process rule.
151	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can edit the gate, logged, not prevented (⚠️ R3.2.2, R3.6 #1;
152	  logging 📖 R3.2.2); alerts on ruleset changes; monthly report of cross-domain approvals. An agent could approve through its engineer's login; no detection found (⚠️). The
153	  required-check app's hosting, key and triggers are open (⚠️ G19).
154	- **Next steps:** rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check in phase 1; the required-check app
155	  before any agent workflow may open PRs; L3 owner team composition open (G17).
156	
157	## 5. References
158	
159	- Framework layer 3 ("Gate = merge to `main`", "Who approves at night"), layer 7 (audit alerts).
160	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0004.
161	=== docs/adr/0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md
162	# ADR-0004: Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview
163	
164	- **Status:** Accepted
165	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
166	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (OD8, OD11, OD13)
167	- **Scope:** deploy workflows for Pulumi and Serverless stacks; k0s and Firebase not covered yet
168	
169	## 1. Context
170	
171	With the gate at merge time (ADR-0003), the approver reviews the code change, not the prod diff. A
172	PR may not preview prod, because that would run PR code with state-write and secret access
173	(📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). So a stateful delete or an IAM change can reach prod without anyone
174	seeing its real effect. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as
175	`serverless.yml`, not in separate L3 paths (assumed ⚠️; we have no access to the repo).
176	
177	## 2. Options considered
178	
179	| Option | Pros | Cons |
180	|---|---|---|
181	| A. Accept the gap | No extra step | Destructive diffs applied unseen |
182	| B. Risk stop, approved by the L3 owner team | Specialist review | Often a third person; L3 team must be on call 24/7 |
183	| C. Risk stop, approved by an owner of the stack | Stays at two people; works at night | Less specialist review; compensated by automated checks |
184	
185	## 3. Decision
186	
187	Option C [design]. The deploy job on `main` previews prod. On stateful replace/delete, an IAM
188	change, a network or security-group change, or (from phase 2) an advisory policy finding, it stops
189	and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a PR (the workflow does not, as "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
190	approve pull requests" stays off, 📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3) adding
191	`deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` with the SHA and preview hash (owned by the stack's owners and the
192	on-call group, OD8, OD9); the first approver approves it
193	(OD13). If that approver is unavailable, another stack owner approves; this makes three people and
194	is recorded as a deviation (OD11). After the merge the workflow previews again on the new HEAD and
195	continues only if the hash matches. Serverless uses `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI because
196	differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2). A `mandatory` Pulumi policy violation always
197	blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2; policy packs from phase 2).
198	
199	## 4. Consequences
200	
201	- **Positive:** the person who approves now sees the prod diff for the changes that can do lasting
202	  damage. Still two people in the normal case.
203	- **Negative / trade-offs:** while a stack is stopped, later deploys to it stop too (the hash
204	  differs), including an incident fix, until the approval lands or the change is reverted. One more review round when the stop fires.
205	- **Risks & how we watch them:** preview output may not be stable enough to hash (⚠️ Options §8); if
206	  not, compare a structured summary. Until phase 2, the risk stop is the only compensation for OD8;
207	  Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and policy packs follow. k0s and Firebase have no
208	  preview step in this design (⚠️ G1, G2).
209	- **Next steps:** risk stop in the deploy job in phase 1.
210	
211	## 5. References
212	
213	- Framework layer 3 ("Risk stop"), layer 5 (required checks); `work/03-options.md` §1.
214	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0003.

216	# ADR-0005: Break-glass is a time-limited, approved JIT grant, for incidents only
217	
218	- **Status:** Accepted
219	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
220	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-8; Options §9 Q2; D2; OD7, OD13)
221	- **Scope:** AWS production accounts through IAM Identity Center; k0s and Firebase not covered (G1, G2)
222	
223	## 1. Context
224	
225	Some incidents cannot use the PR path: GitHub or Actions is down, the pipeline is broken, or the
226	operation is not in IaC and has no runbook. Without a defined fallback, people keep standing access
227	"just in case", which ADR-0002 removes.
228	
229	## 2. Options considered
230	
231	| Option | Pros | Cons |
232	|---|---|---|
233	| A. No fallback | Single path | Outage of GitHub blocks every fix; pressure to keep standing access |
234	| B. Standing break-glass account, used first and approved later | Always available | Standing prod write; unapproved use, rejected by the owner (GĐ-8, Options §0.4) |
235	| C. Approved JIT grant, 1-hour role session, command list, reconciled after | Approval before use; time-boxed; traceable | Approves a command list, not an applied change (partial) |
236	
237	## 3. Decision
238	
239	Option C [design], used only during an incident when the PR path cannot be used.
240	
241	- **Request:** command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub.
242	- **Approval:** the on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; the on-call approver counts as
243	  owner of the service (OD13).
244	- **Grant:** `InfraOperator-<service>` [design name], assigned via `CreateAccountAssignment` and removed
245	  via `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4).
246	- **Execution:** the incident responder types the commands in a terminal without an agent (D2, OD7).
247	- **Example request** (illustrative command ⚠️): "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage.
248	  Run `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
249	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
250	- **After:** CloudTrail writes in the window are compared with the list; a codify PR follows by a
251	  fixed deadline; drift detection runs until it merges.
252	
253	## 4. Consequences
254	
255	- **Positive:** no standing prod write even for emergencies; every use has an approval, a window and
256	  a reconciliation.
257	- **Negative / trade-offs:** meets the approval rule only partly (owner accepted). "No agent in the
258	  JIT terminal" is a process rule: the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
259	- **Risks & how we watch them:** deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions, so a grant
260	  can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which keeps
261	  the user blocked ≥ 12 h (📖 R2.4.4); no night-time path to apply it is designed yet (⚠️ G20).
262	  Metrics: JIT used where a PR was possible, writes outside the list, late codify PRs (review at 1).
263	- **Next steps:** minimal JIT with per-grant CloudTrail comparison and a manual drift check of the
264	  touched stacks in phase 1 (a temporary deviation from D2); revocation SCP and
265	  automated reconciliation in phase 2.
266	
267	## 5. References
268	
269	- Framework layer 7 ("Break-glass = JIT fallback"); `work/03-options.md` §4b, §9.
270	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0002.
271	=== docs/adr/0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md
272	# ADR-0006: MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue
273	
274	- **Status:** Accepted
275	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
276	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framework approval 2026-11-09; rollout priority framing Q8)
277	- **Scope:** Claude Code on all engineer laptops and in CI; Papaya's internal plugin marketplace
278	
279	## 1. Context
280	
281	Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP
282	servers receive tokens and data. Papaya runs an internal plugin marketplace (brief, Appendix A), and
283	engineers install MCP servers without review (brief); use of Linear and Slack through MCP is assumed
284	(⚠️ G9). An unreviewed server or a plugin update can read the repo, the SSO cache or claim
285	data and send it out.
286	
287	## 2. Options considered
288	
289	| Option | Pros | Cons |
290	|---|---|---|
291	| A. Free choice, guidance only | No friction | No inventory; any server can exfiltrate |
292	| B. Denylist known-bad servers | Low friction | Misses new and changed servers |
293	| C. Allowlist (catalogue) enforced by managed settings | Inventory and supplier records; blocks unknown servers | Up to 5 working days' wait for a new tool (S6) |
294	
295	## 3. Decision
296	
297	Option C. The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team.
298	
299	- **Plugins:** only Papaya's marketplace via managed `strictKnownMarketplaces`, plus
300	  `blockedMarketplaces` (📖 R1.4.2); sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only);
301	  `disableSideloadFlags` (📖 R1.4.2); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
302	- **MCP:** `allowedMcpServers` with `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4); match by
303	  `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` (exact argv), never `serverName`, which "is not a security control"
304	  (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7).
305	- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher, local or remote, what it reads and where it sends data,
306	  supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2), pinned version.
307	  Example entry: `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` [design; placeholder].
308	- **CI:** server-managed settings do not reach a CI job (📖 R1.7.10); CI uses a managed-settings
309	  file on the runner and a fixed MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
310	  (📖 R1.3.5).
311	
312	## 4. Consequences
313	
314	- **Positive:** Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier records (P4c); unknown servers are
315	  refused before they load.
316	- **Negative / trade-offs:** waiting time for new tools; review effort for 1–2 DevSecOps people.
317	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the enforced copy lives in server-managed settings, edited in the
318	  admin console by Owners, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports and diffs it with git monthly until
319	  G18 is solved (ADR-0007). `disableSideloadFlags` does not cover `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`
320	  (📖 R1.4.2), so the MCP allowlist must be locked. No per-group targeting in server-managed settings
321	  (📖 R1.1.6). Tool description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️). Without MDM, laptops can
322	  bypass server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). Evidence: OTel `plugin_installed` /
323	  `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6).
324	- **Next steps:** catalogue v1 in phase 1 (may slip to phase 2 only with owner agreement).
325	
326	## 5. References
327	
328	- Framework layer 4; layer 8 rollout.
329	- Related: ADR-0007.
330	=== docs/adr/0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md
331	# ADR-0007: Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary
332	
333	- **Status:** Accepted
334	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
335	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-6, Options §0.4; D1, D3; OD4, OD7b, OD12)
336	- **Scope:** Claude Code on laptops (server-managed settings, Team plan) and in CI
337	
338	## 1. Context
339	
340	The brief names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem. It is tempting to make Claude Code
341	settings the main control. But server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not a security
342	boundary" (📖 R1.1.7), local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8), Bash rules are not a boundary
343	(📖 R1.2.6), and on laptops without MDM another login or provider skips server-managed settings
344	(📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11).
345	
346	## 2. Options considered
347	
348	| Option | Pros | Cons |
349	|---|---|---|
350	| 0. Today (brief): some engineers turn prompts off; no organization policy is described (P3c) | No friction | Prompts turned off unnoticed; no evidence |
351	| A. Settings as the boundary (lock everything, block auto mode) | Simple story | Bypassable on laptops; high friction; people work around it |
352	| B. Settings as hygiene; IAM and the CI gate as the boundary | Boundary holds even if settings are bypassed | Settings give weaker guarantees than they appear to |
353	
354	## 3. Decision
355	
356	Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
357	uniform defaults:
358	
359	- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
360	  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
361	- `permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
362	- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` in
363	  `sandbox.excludedCommands` [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
364	- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).
365	
366	Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
367	CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
368	(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).
369	
370	Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
371	OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).
372	
373	## 4. Consequences
374	
375	- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read AWS PHI
376	  stores with the engineer's standing identity, once standing write is removed (PHI paths outside IAM
377	  are process-only, ADR-0009). Compliance gets
378	  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
379	- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
380	  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
381	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
382	  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
383	  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
384	  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
385	  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
386	  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
387	  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference): repo code that the agent can edit (Pulumi programs, Serverless
388	  plugins) then runs with network and `~/.aws`, and SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by
389	  ADR-0002. With OD12, Manual mode does not mean a prompt for every command (📖 R5.5.5b).
390	- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.
391	
392	## 5. References
393	
394	- Framework layer 2; layer 8 rollout; research 6.6 (D1–D3).
395	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
396	=== docs/adr/0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md
397	# ADR-0008: CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception
398	
399	- **Status:** Accepted
400	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
401	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framing Q8; OD1, OD6; target S2)
402	- **Scope:** GitHub Actions deploy workflows to AWS, GCP, k0s and Firebase
403	
404	## 1. Context
405	
406	CI becomes the only routine production writer (ADR-0001), so it is the main target. Repository
407	secrets can be read by anyone with write access (📖 R3.5.3b), which, in the single monorepo, likely includes every engineer (⚠️ assumed) and their
408	agent. A long-lived key there is standing prod write in disguise.
409	
410	## 2. Options considered
411	
412	| Option | Pros | Cons |
413	|---|---|---|
414	| A. Keep stored keys, rotate them | No migration | Standing prod write for all writers |
415	| B. OIDC everywhere, no exception | S2 = 0 | k0s and Firebase may not support it yet (G1, G2) |
416	| C. OIDC for AWS and GCP; a controlled exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials | Removes most keys now | One exception to manage |
417	
418	## 3. Decision
419	
420	Option C.
421	
422	- **AWS:** GitHub OIDC (📖 R3.4.1); the prod role trusts only the `production` environment of the
423	  monorepo (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4), ideally narrowed by `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
424	- **GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization (📖 R3.4.5b).
425	- **k0s/Firebase exception** (OD1, OD6): CI deploy credentials only, until it is checked whether they
426	  can use OIDC. Conditions [design]: a `production` environment secret, never a repository secret
427	  (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3); GitHub-hosted runners, because on self-hosted runners environment secrets act
428	  like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5); if k0s needs a self-hosted runner, it is dedicated to the
429	  `production` deploy and the residual risk is recorded (⚠️ G15); a single source of truth; owner, expiry, rotation.
430	- `GITHUB_TOKEN` default "restricted" (📖 R3.5.3); actions pinned by lockfile or full SHA (📖 R3.5.5).
431	
432	## 4. Consequences
433	
434	- **Positive:** no stored AWS or GCP keys to leak (S2); every deploy credential is tied to a reviewed
435	  workflow on `main`.
436	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one-time migration; slower action updates. The exception remains until
437	  G1/G2 are solved.
438	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can change or delete the environment, and a deleted
439	  environment comes back without protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); alerts and a settings comparison cover it.
440	  The GitHub Apps used for CI agents and the required check have their own keys (⚠️ G19).
441	  Runtime credentials inside the cluster are out of the exception (OD6).
442	- **Next steps:** OIDC and removal of stored keys in phase 1; k0s/Firebase credentials moved to
443	  environment secrets before standing prod write is removed.
444	
445	## 5. References
446	
447	- Framework layer 1 ("CI → AWS", "CI → GCP"), layer 5 ("Credentials").
448	- Related: ADR-0001.
449	=== docs/adr/0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md
450	# ADR-0009: The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant
451	
452	- **Status:** Accepted
453	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
454	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (research 1.9, 5.8 "not extended"; GĐ-9, GĐ-14)
455	- **Scope:** coding-agent sessions on laptops and in CI; production stores of all insurer tenants
456	
457	## 1. Context
458	
459	Papaya holds medical records, national IDs and bank accounts for several insurer tenants in
460	different countries. Claude Team is not shown as BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Partner-uploaded claim
461	documents are both PHI and a prompt-injection vector (research 1.11.4 L6). Neither OWASP nor NIST
462	knows a full prevention for prompt injection (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
463	
464	## 2. Options considered
465	
466	| Option | Pros | Cons |
467	|---|---|---|
468	| A. Agent reads prod data freely | Fastest debugging | PHI in transcripts; injection can exfiltrate; no BAA |
469	| B. Agent never reads any customer data | Simplest rule | Blocks legitimate debugging of non-PHI data |
470	| C. Agent outside PHI; other personal data case by case under an approved, per-tenant grant | Matches the owner's boundary; debugging still possible | Process controls on some paths |
471	
472	## 3. Decision
473	
474	Option C.
475	
476	- **PHI:** never in an agent session. A human reads in a terminal without an agent and gives the
477	  agent a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
478	  it [design].
479	- **Other personal data:** readable within an approved request naming one tenant, purpose, store,
480	  window and agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9); approved by an approver ≠ requester and
481	  co-approved by the tenant's data owner [design]; data-read role, 1 h [design]. The same request
482	  applies when a human reads PHI. At night the
483	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day [design].
484	- **Partner documents:** reproduced with synthetic documents or de-identified first [design].
485	- **Non-prod:** synthetic or masked only (GĐ-14); no prod copies (S11).
486	
487	This is a target, not a guarantee: "no agent in the PHI terminal" is a process rule [design] with
488	the same weakness as D2, since the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
489	
490	## 4. Consequences
491	
492	- **Positive:** "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2); one record per
493	  exception (S9). Assumes injection succeeds and limits what it can reach.
494	- **Negative / trade-offs:** debugging with redacted or synthetic data; a request for each real read.
495	- **Risks & how we watch them:** of the 17 paths to PHI (research 1.11.4), tickets, chat, pasted text,
496	  admin pages, CI logs, prod AI traces and fixtures are covered by process only; k0s and GCP stores follow the same principle
497	  with mechanisms still open (G1, G3). Per-tenant scoping through session tags (📖 R2.1.8) is
498	  unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️). During a data-read window a stolen SSO
499	  token could open the grant (⚠️, ADR-0007). Data-plane deny actions are incomplete (⚠️ G13). Planted-injection test in
500	  phase 3.
501	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and the minimal real-data read flow in phase 1; data-plane SCP in
502	  phase 2.
503	
504	## 5. References
505	
506	- Framework layer 6; layer 1 (SCPs); research 1.9, 1.11.4, 5.8.
507	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
508	=== docs/adr/0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md
509	# ADR-0010: Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval
510	
511	- **Status:** Accepted
512	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
513	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-14; OD2, OD3, OD8, OD9, OD13)
514	- **Scope:** every change made by engineers and their agents, from non-prod to production
515	
516	## 1. Context
517	
518	Engineering says "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly" (brief); the need is speed. Compliance's
519	sentence covers production writes only (framing §3.1). A single rule for all changes either slows non-prod for
520	no gain or leaves high-risk prod changes with too light a review. The owner also wants every prod
521	change to need two people, no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it (OD2).
522	
523	## 2. Options considered
524	
525	| Option | Pros | Cons |
526	|---|---|---|
527	| A. Same approval for everything | Simple | Non-prod loop slowed for no gain; high-risk changes get no extra scrutiny |
528	| B. More approvers as risk grows (e.g. two for L3) | More eyes on dangerous changes | Breaks the two-person rule; slower incidents |
529	| C. Risk level narrows who may approve, plus a risk stop; non-prod free | Fast where damage is small; specialist owners where it is large | One reviewer for high-risk changes can miss things |
530	
531	## 3. Decision
532	
533	Option C [design levels]:
534	
535	| Level | What | Approval |
536	|---|---|---|
537	| L0 | Reads: non-prod anything, prod metadata | none |
538	| L1 | Changes in non-prod (synthetic or masked data only, GĐ-14) | none, author only |
539	| L2 | Routine prod change, e.g. Lambda memory 1024 → 2048 MB | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher |
540	| L3 | IAM/SCP, stateful replace/delete, network, workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, advisory policy finding (full list: framework layer 5) | 1 owner of that path |
541	| L3-JIT | Break-glass in an incident | on-call approver ≠ requester (ADR-0005) |
542	| L3-data | Real customer data read | approver ≠ requester + agreement; data-owner co-approval [design] (ADR-0009) |
543	
544	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent-configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for the
545	whole team (OD3). Process-defining paths and the SCP stack are owned by the L3 owner team; IAM or
546	stateful changes inside a domain file are approved by that stack's owners (OD8, OD13). At every level,
547	the risk stop applies to any deploy whose prod diff is risky (ADR-0004).
548	
549	## 4. Consequences
550	
551	- **Positive:** a free non-prod loop for engineers and agents (S4); the same two-person rule for every
552	  prod change, incidents included (three people only by recorded deviation, OD11). Compliance gets a written rule for who may approve what.
553	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one approver for high-risk changes (owner's trade-off for speed);
554	  `CLAUDE.md` edits wait for the L3 owner team, not the domain team that edits them most.
555	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the free loop holds only if non-prod has no real data; a non-prod
556	  store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule until scanned (S11). A risky diff hidden in an L2 PR is
557	  caught by the risk stop, not by the level (Pulumi and Serverless stacks only;
558	  k0s and Firebase have none yet, G1, G2).
559	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and CODEOWNERS with the L3 path list in phase 1; composition of
560	  the L3 owner team is open (G17).
561	
562	## 5. References
563	
564	- Framework layer 3 (levels table), layer 5 (canonical L3 path list), layer 6 (non-prod).
565	- Related: ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0009.
566	=== docs/adr/0012-approval-integrity-checked-by-the-gate-app.md
567	# ADR-0012: Approval integrity is checked by the approval-gate app: two approvals on process paths, on-call approvals only for open incidents
568	
569	- **Status:** Accepted; supersedes in part ADR-0003 (domain review on normal days as a process rule; one approval for cross-team PRs, OD10) and ADR-0010 (one approver for L3 process paths)
570	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
571	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission, after the independent review (`work/07-review.md`; OD26, OD27)
572	- **Scope:** pull requests to `main` of the monorepo; the `approval-gate` required check
573	
574	## 1. Context
575	
576	ADR-0003 made the merge to `main` the approval gate, with an on-call group that co-owns every
577	deployable path, so that one primary can approve any fix at night. GitHub accepts an approval from
578	any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve any domain's PR, and the
579	`incident` label that was meant to limit this can be applied by anyone with Triage (📖 R9.1.9).
580	ADR-0010 kept one approver for every level. The review also found that a compromised plugin or
581	local MCP server runs on every laptop and could give an attacker many GitHub logins at once
582	(threat T23), so a single approval on the files that define the process is one stolen login away.
583	A path-scoped reviewer rule was not found for GitHub Team (📖 R9.1.15), and the ruleset's approval
584	count is repository-wide.
585	
586	## 2. Options considered
587	
588	| Option | Pros | Cons |
589	|---|---|---|
590	| A. Keep process rules and the monthly report | No new logic | The label is free to apply; the report misses labelled PRs; one login changes the process |
591	| B. Raise the ruleset to two approvals for every PR | Built into GitHub | Doubles review for every change, against S4 and the owner's two-person rule |
592	| C. The approval-gate app, already required, checks the rules per file | Exact rules per path; works on Team | More logic in a custom app that every merge depends on (G19) |
593	
594	## 3. Decision
595	
596	Option C [design]. The app's decision logic is examples E12 (`examples/approval-gate/gate.py`):
597	
598	- an approval counts only if it is on the head commit, by a human who is not the author, the last
599	  pusher or the person who triggered an app-opened PR (📖 R9.1.10 for the review fields);
600	- every changed file needs a counted approval from one of its owner teams;
601	- an on-call group member's approval counts for another team's file only if the PR carries the
602	  `incident` label, links an incident that is open when the check runs, and the approver is on
603	  shift (OD27);
604	- a file owned only by the L3 owner team (a process path) needs two different members of that
605	  team (OD26);
606	- approvals within two minutes of the last push, or at night without an incident, are flagged for
607	  the monthly report, not blocked.
608	
609	## 4. Consequences
610	
611	- **Positive:** domain review on normal days and the two-person rule on process paths are enforced,
612	  not trained; the incident lane cannot be opened by a label alone; flagged approvals give a
613	  detection signal for rubber-stamping and stolen logins.
614	- **Negative / trade-offs:** process-path PRs need two L3 owner team members; a cross-team PR on a
615	  normal day needs an owner of each team (OD10's single approval now holds only in incidents);
616	  a stale schedule or incident record blocks a night approval until the backup or a domain owner
617	  approves; every merge depends more on the app.
618	- **Risks & how we watch them:** if the app is down, every merge is blocked, incident PRs included,
619	  and the JIT fallback applies (layer 7); its hosting, key and triggers stay open (G19); the schedule
620	  file is an L3 path; the monthly report lists every `incident` PR and every flagged approval.
621	- **Next steps:** the app becomes a hard prerequisite in phase 1, before the ruleset requires its
622	  check (rollout).
623	
624	## 5. References
625	
626	- Framework layer 3 ("L3 approvals", "Who approves at night"), layer 4 ("Pinning what every
627	  laptop runs"), layer 7 (on-call); threat model T7, T23.
628	- Related: ADR-0003, ADR-0006, ADR-0010.
629	=== docs/adr/README.md
630	# Architecture decision records
631	
632	Each record states one major decision behind [`../01-framework.md`](../01-framework.md), the options weighed
633	and what it costs. The reasoning and its sources live in the framework, audit evidence in
634	[`../04-compliance-mapping.md`](../04-compliance-mapping.md); an ADR only records the choice. Markers follow the framework legend: 📖 R*x.y* = documented research row in
635	`work/02-research.md`, ⚠️ = inference or unverified, [design] = proposal of this submission. OD*n* = owner
636	decisions in the framework's last table; D1–D3 = owner decisions in research 6.6. Other codes (GĐ-n
637	assumptions, S-n success criteria, P-n problems, G-n gaps, Options §n, framing §n) are explained in the
638	framework's "How to read this" section.
639	
640	| ADR | Decision | Framework layer |
641	|---|---|---|
642	| [0001](0001-prod-changes-only-through-ci.md) | Every production change goes through a reviewed PR applied by CI ("IaC first") | 3, 5 |
643	| [0002](0002-no-standing-prod-write-read-only-agent-identity.md) | Nobody holds standing prod write; in prod the only standing role (the engineer's, so the agent's) reads metadata | 1, 2 |
644	| [0003](0003-merge-to-main-is-the-approval-gate.md) | The merge to `main` is the approval gate: two people, code owners, on-call co-ownership (superseded in part by 0012) | 3 |
645	| [0004](0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md) | Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview | 3 |
646	| [0005](0005-break-glass-is-time-limited-jit.md) | Break-glass is a time-limited, approved JIT grant, for incidents only | 7 |
647	| [0006](0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md) | MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue | 4 |
648	| [0007](0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md) | Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary | 2 |
649	| [0008](0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md) | CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception | 1, 5 |
650	| [0009](0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md) | The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant | 1, 6 |
651	| [0010](0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md) | Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval (superseded in part by 0012) | 3 |
652	| [0012](0012-approval-integrity-checked-by-the-gate-app.md) | The approval-gate app checks approval integrity: two approvals on process paths, on-call approvals only for open incidents | 3, 4 |
653

655	monthly reconciliation, drift detection; framework layer 7), the rollout plan
656	([`../03-rollout-plan.md`](../03-rollout-plan.md)) and the CI-agent setup
657	(layer 5; covered in parts by ADR-0006 and ADR-0007).
658

660	
661	## Refinements since acceptance
662	
663	Writing and testing the files in [`../../examples/`](../../examples/README.md) made some details more
664	precise. None changes a decision, so no ADR is superseded; the framework carries the current wording.
665	
666	- **ADR-0003:** "merge approval = deploy approval" gains two conditions: squash-only merges (OD16)
667	  and deploying only the current tip of `main`, because a writer can re-run an old deploy run for
668	  30 days and roll prod back without approval (OD17; examples finding 4).
669	- **ADR-0004:** "the approver sees the prod diff" means the approver sees **which** prod resources and
670	  properties change, not the new values, which stay out of the job summary so that secrets stay out of
671	  logs; values are reviewed in the code of the stopped PR. The approval is also bound to git history
672	  (examples E7, finding 2), and an early approval can match a later change outside the stack, an
673	  accepted gap until G19 (OD18).
674	- **ADR-0007:** the "read-only allowlist" became two exact repo scripts, because Claude Code already runs
675	  read-only commands without a prompt and wildcard rules can write files (examples finding 19); phase 1
676	  adds a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell` (OD21). `sandbox.excludedCommands`
677	  entries need a trailing ` *` and are paired with `ask` rules, so each excluded CLI call prompts, auto
678	  mode included (examples finding 22).
679	
680	After the independent review (`work/07-review.md`; owner decisions from OD22, 2026-11-09). Two
681	changes are decisions and got their own ADR: ADR-0011 (database changes) and ADR-0012, which
682	supersedes parts of ADR-0003 and ADR-0010. The others narrow how a decision is carried out:
683	
684	- **ADR-0002:** "nobody holds standing prod write" now also covers who administers Identity Center:
685	  permission sets and assignments are code owned by the L3 owner team only, other changes raise an
686	  alert, `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` is denied in the prod OU and member-account root
687	  credentials are removed (OD23). The management account stays outside SCPs: detected, not prevented.
688	- **ADR-0003 / ADR-0004:** what runs in the deploy job is limited from phase 1: one GitHub
689	  environment per kind of stack (`production-iam` for the IAM stack), bounded domain deploy roles,
690	  no install scripts except a reviewed allowlist, and an agent review on infrastructure PRs (OD22).
691	  This was OD20's phase-2 roadmap item. The risk stop's scope is unchanged (OD15).
692	- **ADR-0008:** the k0s exception gets conditions: a separate `production-k0s` environment (was
693	  optional), a namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token instead of a kubeconfig, and the
694	  Kubernetes API audit log; target is k0s trusting GitHub OIDC directly (OD24).
695	- **ADR-0006:** "pinned catalogue" now covers what reaches every laptop: the marketplace is pinned
696	  to a protected release tag, every plugin (internal ones too) to a commit, auto-update is off, and
697	  local MCP servers are admitted only as immutable artifacts (OD26).
698	- **ADR-0003 / ADR-0007:** managed deny rules for `gh pr review` and the `gh` token file from phase 1,
699	  as hygiene behind OD5; a login register maps GitHub accounts to people (OD25). The parts of
700	  ADR-0003 that ADR-0012 supersedes are listed in ADR-0012.
